Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class WindowSnap

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.WindowSnap
public final class WindowSnap extends Object
The pure geometry of window snapping on the 2D/Swing desktop: given the pointer position while a window is being dragged and the desktop bounds, it decides which edge (if any) the window should snap to and the rectangle it should occupy there.

Dragging a window's title bar against the left or right edge snaps it to that half of the desktop; dragging it against the top edge maximises it. This mirrors the snap-to-edge behaviour of a conventional desktop window manager, which the MDI JDesktopPane does not provide on its own.

Because it is desktop-agnostic, the native 3D desktop reuses the same zone vocabulary and the same half/maximise target rule through the float (zoneForRect/boundsForRect) overloads below, which work in world units on a dragged Frame3D's bounding rectangle instead of a pointer in pixels; org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.snap is the 3D glue that feeds them.

This class is pure geometry with no Swing, painting or Java 3D, so the snap decision is unit-testable headless; SnappingDesktopManager and SnapPreview are the thin Swing glue that consume it.

  • Method Details

    • zoneForRect

      public static WindowSnap.Zone zoneForRect(float left, float top, float right, float bottom, float screenLeft, float screenTop, float screenRight, float screenBottom, float threshold)
      The snap zone for a dragged window's bounding rectangle, in any consistent unit (the 3D desktop passes world units). The rectangle is given as (left, top, right, bottom) with top > bottom (a y-up space) and the screen the same way; the top edge wins over the side edges so dragging into the top corner maximises rather than half-snaps. Returns WindowSnap.Zone.NONE for degenerate inputs or a rectangle away from every edge.
      Parameters:
      threshold - the edge proximity, in the same unit, that triggers a snap

    • boundsForRect

      public static float[] boundsForRect(WindowSnap.Zone zone, float screenLeft, float screenTop, float screenRight, float screenBottom)
      The rectangle a window occupies when snapped to zone, as {left, top, width, height} in the same unit and orientation as zoneForRect(float, float, float, float, float, float, float, float, float). The left/right halves split the screen width exactly; MAXIMIZE returns the whole screen. Returns null for WindowSnap.Zone.NONE or a degenerate screen.

    • centreOf
